DOCX post-processors

Source: R/report_docx.R
pub_pp_docx.Rd

Post-processors of DOCX reports (see post_process in pub_report_spec()) that write the header and footer lines and lock them.

Usage

pub_pp_docx_header_footer(header = NULL, footer = NULL)

pub_pp_docx_lock()

Arguments

header, footer

Named character vector of lines like the document's metadata header and footer (names left, center, right), or NULL (use the document's lines). A vector replaces the document's lines as a whole; character() writes none.

Value

A post-processor: function(path, doc, spec) that changes the DOCX file path in place (doc is the document with the render-time metadata).

Details

Functions

  • pub_pp_docx_header_footer() writes the header and footer lines of the document into the header and footer of the file, as the PDF report shows them.

  • pub_pp_docx_lock() locks the headers and footers against accidental editing and deletion.

pub_render() applies both to every DOCX report (the lock if the spec's lock is TRUE), before the spec's own post-processors. To give one of them other arguments or another place among the others, list it in the spec's post_process. It is then not added again (see Examples).

Header and footer lines

The lines are the entries header and footer of the document's metadata (see pub_doc()), each with the parts left, center and right. A part goes into the bookmark of the same name in the file: header_left, header_center, header_right, footer_left, footer_center or footer_right.

  • {trace} becomes the trace stamp (see pub_trace_stamp()) and line breaks become spaces.

  • The text takes the format of the first run in the bookmark that has one.

  • It goes into every header and footer of the file that has the bookmark. Settings of the reference document (e.g. different first or even pages) are kept.

  • A part that isn't empty is an error if no header or footer has its bookmark.

  • In pubflow's reference document, footer_right holds "Page x / N". So a right footer line replaces the page number, as in PDF (an empty one removes it).

Locks

pub_pp_docx_lock() locks everything in every header and footer, also the content of the reference document such as "Page x / N". Tables and figures are locked by pub_markdown() itself: with the spec's lock = TRUE all but those with pub_set_meta(locked = FALSE), otherwise those with pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE). Applying the post-processor twice changes nothing.

The locks only guard against accidental changes: Word lets users remove them in the properties of a content control.

See also

pub_report_spec(), pub_render(), pub_trace_stamp()

Examples

doc <- pub_doc(meta = list(
    author = "Jane Doe",
    time = as.POSIXct("2026-10-08 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
    footer = c(left = "{trace}")
))
# A DOCX file with the bookmarks: a copy of pubflow's reference document
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
file.copy(system.file("templates", "reference.docx", package = "pubflow"),
          path)
#> [1] TRUE
fill <- pub_pp_docx_header_footer(header = c(left = "Draft",
                                             right = "Batch A"))
fill(path, doc, pub_report_spec("docx"))

# In a spec: another header in DOCX reports, the lock after the spec's
# own post-processor
log_file <- function(path, doc, spec) message("Rendered ", path)
spec <- pub_report_spec("docx", post_process = list(
    pub_pp_docx_header_footer(header = c(left = "Draft")),
    log_file,
    pub_pp_docx_lock()
))
spec
#> <pubflow report spec: docx>
#>   reference_docx    default
#>   front_matter      title block
#>   toc               depth 3
#>   number_sections   yes
#>   page              reference document
#>   figure            default
#>   labels            Table, Figure
#>   lock              marked items
#>   error_items       refuse
#>   post_process      3 function(s)
#>   pandoc_args       none
